newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Treasury sets new bonds as SNB eases.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Treasury sets new bonds as SNB eases.

text.p: The Swiss Treasury successfully launched two tranches of government bonds on Thursday, with bidding ending barely a minute before the Swiss National Bank announced it was cutting its discount rate.
"It (the rate cut) was a surprise, and I have a feeling the markets were surprised as well," said Peter Thomann, head of the Swiss Federal Treasury in an interview with Reuters.
The latest auction was the last one scheduled for 1996 with a payment date in the current year. The next auction is scheduled for November 28, with payment on January 7.

Thomann did not rule out further, unscheduled auctions before the end of the year but he said the Swiss government has already nearly met its borrowing target of 5.00 billion Swiss francs for this year.

"We, of course, reserve the right to bring an issue outside of the issue programme if we feel that would be necessary. But I must say that we have almost reached the (goal) of five billion Swiss francs gross," Thomann said.
Thomann said the Treasury may not have planned to issue so much this year. "That was not our goal, but we increased these (latest) bonds because the yields were very interesting for us," he added.

The results of the auction were released after the SNB's announcement it was lowering its discount rate to 1.0 percent from 1.50 percent, bringing the key rate back to historic lows last seen when it was cut to that level in Feburary 1978.
The latest issue comprised a reopening of a 4-1/4 percent January 2008 bond, and a reopening of a 5-1/2 percent January 2005 bond.

The larger tranche maturing in 2008 had a total allocation of 1.0 billion Swiss francs, which is large for a Confederate bond. The offering was priced at 100.60 to yield 4.18 percent. Total bids were 1,598.9 billion Swiss francs.
"The interest rate is completely in the market," said Thomann of the longer tranche. He said that the price level on the new bond was "relatively interesting for us."
"There were also very large single price classes, with as much as 400 million Swiss francs in one price class," he said.
"We also had the impression that we had to serve the market, to provide liquidity in this bond. Evidently there is a demand for longer maturities," he said.
With respect to the shorter tranche maturing in 2005, Thomann said the volume in the bond before it was reopened was less than one billion francs.
"We had the impression that we should do something to provide liquidity in this issue," said Thomann.
He said that Swiss institutional investors, especially insurers, need to have a coupon of at least 4.00 percent.
He said these investors were therefore more interested in paying a price above par, and getting a higher coupon.
"A coupon of 5-1/2 percent is high for the market," he said, but added the issue also offered an opportunity for write-offs in view of large gains from share markets.
"In view of that we would have expected more interest, but perhaps the price is a bit high," he said.
The shorter tranche will also be deliverable against the medium-term "comi" futures contract next year. The comi contract was launched on the Soffex exchange in June.
